column28: Students using AI to write code, and make inferences about results. This is fine if they have a good understanding of the underlying principles to begin with, as they can guide the AI and see where it may be right or wrong. But if students use AI to skip the learning and understanding part, then they are 'driving blindfolded'. They won't actually learn anything, and may even go wrong. So, responsible and intellectually engaged use of AI is good, but mindless AI copy/paste is bad.
